note: Curated MVP knowledge base. Summaries and skills paraphrased from O*NET OnLine (U.S. DoL); outlook categories and transition notes are founding-team curation informed by O*NET related-occupations data. Illustrative for the MVP — refresh before any production use.

entries.title: Software Engineer
entries.summary: Designs, builds, and maintains software systems. Value concentrates in system design, code quality, and the ability to translate ambiguous requirements into working products.

transitionsFrom.note: Analysts with strong scripting move via data engineering; gap is software craft (testing, design patterns).

outlook.note: Sustained demand, but commodity feature work is increasingly automated; differentiation shifts to system design and product judgment.

entries.title: Engineering Manager
entries.summary: Leads software teams: hiring, delivery, technical direction, and people development. The pivot from engineer is a shift from personal output to team leverage.

transitionsFrom.note: Classic path; the gap is people skills and letting go of hands-on coding. Usually requires senior-level credibility first.

outlook.note: Tracks engineering headcount; mid-management layers thin in downturns.

entries.title: Product Manager
entries.summary: Owns what gets built and why: customer discovery, prioritization, roadmap, and cross-functional delivery. Rewards synthesis, communication, and commercial judgment over deep specialism.

transitionsFrom.note: Common path; gap is customer discovery and roadmap ownership rather than technical depth.
Feasible via fintech or internal-tools PM roles; gap is product craft and shipped-product evidence. An internal transfer or APM program de-risks it.
Designers move via product sense; gap is commercial ownership and analytics.

outlook.note: Demand solid for PMs who pair customer insight with data fluency; entry-level PM openings remain competitive.

entries.title: Data Analyst
entries.summary: Turns raw data into decisions: queries, dashboards, experiment readouts, and business narratives. A common launchpad role with several strong upward paths.

transitionsFrom.note: Skill overlap is high (Excel/SQL/modeling); gap is usually modern BI tooling.

outlook.note: Pure reporting is being automated; analysts who own decisions and experiments stay in demand.

entries.title: Data Scientist
entries.summary: Builds statistical and machine-learning models to predict and explain behavior. Increasingly split between ML engineering and decision science tracks.

transitionsFrom.note: Well-trodden path; gap is ML fundamentals and software engineering rigor. Portfolio projects plus internal modeling work usually bridge it.

outlook.note: Strong demand, but the bar has risen: production ML skills matter more than notebook analysis.

entries.title: UX Designer
entries.summary: Designs how products work for people: research, flows, prototypes, and interface systems. Value shifts toward end-to-end product thinking as AI compresses production work.

transitionsFrom.note: Content people move via UX writing and research; gap is interaction design craft.

outlook.note: Junior production design is contracting; strategic/research-led design holds value.

entries.title: Financial Analyst
entries.summary: Builds models and analyses that guide investment and business decisions: forecasting, valuation, variance analysis, and reporting.

transitionsFrom.note: Accountants move via FP&A; gap is forward-looking modeling versus historical reporting.

outlook.note: Core analysis is being augmented by AI tooling; analysts who own business partnering stay valuable.

entries.title: Accountant / Auditor
entries.summary: Prepares and verifies financial records, ensures compliance, and increasingly advises on controls and systems. Credential-gated (CA/CPA equivalents).

outlook.note: Routine bookkeeping automates; advisory, controls, and judgment-heavy audit work persists.

entries.title: Investment Associate
entries.summary: Evaluates investment opportunities: diligence, modeling, market analysis. High-intensity, credential- and network-sensitive path.

transitionsFrom.note: Competitive; typically needs deal exposure, an MBA/CFA signal, or a strong referral network.

outlook.note: Cyclical hiring; junior modeling work is compressing while sourcing and judgment roles persist.

entries.title: Risk Analyst
entries.summary: Identifies and quantifies financial, credit, and operational risk; builds monitoring frameworks and stress tests. Regulation keeps demand steady.

transitionsFrom.note: Quantitative overlap is high; gap is domain regulation and risk frameworks.

outlook.note: Regulatory and model-risk demand growing, including AI-model governance.

entries.title: FP&A Manager
entries.summary: Leads budgeting, forecasting, and management reporting; partners with business leaders on resource decisions. Natural step up from analyst roles.

transitionsFrom.note: Standard promotion path after 4–7 years; gap is stakeholder leadership, not technicals.

outlook.note: Consolidating but resilient; business-partnering skill is the differentiator.

entries.title: Fintech Product Manager
entries.summary: Product management applied to financial products: payments, lending, wealth, or infrastructure. Values domain knowledge of money movement and regulation alongside product craft.

transitionsFrom.note: The most realistic finance→product bridge: domain knowledge transfers, product craft must be built. Internal fintech moves beat cold applications.
Lateral with domain ramp-up.

outlook.note: Fintech hiring recovered selectively; domain-literate PMs are scarce.

entries.title: Digital Marketing Manager
entries.summary: Plans and runs digital acquisition and lifecycle programs: paid, SEO/content, email, and analytics. AI tooling is reshaping execution work toward strategy and measurement.

transitionsFrom.note: Common step; gap is paid channels and analytics rigor.

outlook.note: Execution roles compressing under AI tools; measurement-literate strategists remain in demand.

entries.title: Brand Manager
entries.summary: Owns a brand's positioning, campaigns, and P&L contribution; classic CPG-style general-management track.

transitionsFrom.note: Digital people bring measurement skills; gap is classical brand strategy and P&L exposure.

outlook.note: Fewer, broader roles; strong as a general-management feeder.

entries.title: Content Strategist
entries.summary: Plans and governs content across channels: editorial strategy, information architecture, and voice. AI raises output volume, raising the premium on strategy and editing judgment.

outlook.note: Pure production roles shrinking; strategy/ops hybrids holding.

entries.title: Management Consultant
entries.summary: Solves business problems for clients: analysis, structuring, and change delivery. Prestigious accelerator role with heavy travel/hours trade-offs.

transitionsFrom.note: Analytical overlap strong; entry is credential- and network-gated (target-school or experienced-hire tracks).
Ops leaders enter as experienced hires in operations practices.

outlook.note: Junior analytical layers compressing under AI; client leadership and implementation skills persist.

entries.title: Operations Manager
entries.summary: Runs the machinery of a business: processes, teams, vendors, and performance. Breadth-heavy role whose next steps depend on picking a spike (scale, systems, or P&L).

transitionsFrom.note: CS leaders move into ops via process and team scale.

outlook.note: Always needed, rarely scarce; differentiation comes from systems/automation fluency.

entries.title: Customer Success Manager
entries.summary: Owns retention and expansion for SaaS accounts: onboarding, adoption, renewals. A common entry into tech for relationship-strong professionals.

transitionsFrom.note: Customer-facing overlap; gap is product depth and commercial renewals.

outlook.note: Consolidating toward fewer, more commercial roles; product-fluent CSMs preferred.
